_meta.indication: Adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) experiencing "off" episodes.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, parallel-group, placebo- and active (entacapone)-controlled study of 14-15 week duration.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Parkinson's disease experiencing "off" episodes, treated with levodopa/DOPA decarboxylase inhibitor (alone or in combination with other PD medications).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in mean absolute OFF-time from baseline to endpoint based on 24-hour patient diaries.
pivotal_trials.n: n=600 randomized; ITT ONGENTYS 50 mg n=115, placebo n=120.
pivotal_trials.result: ONGENTYS 50 mg significantly reduced absolute OFF-time vs placebo: LS mean change -1.95 vs -0.93 hours; placebo-subtracted difference -1.01 hours (95% CI -1.620, -0.407); p=0.002.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, parallel-group, placebo-controlled study of 14-15 week duration.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Parkinson's disease experiencing "off" episodes, treated with levodopa/DOPA decarboxylase inhibitor.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in mean absolute OFF-time from baseline to endpoint based on 24-hour patient diaries.
pivotal_trials.n: n=427 randomized; ITT ONGENTYS 50 mg n=147, placebo n=135.
pivotal_trials.result: ONGENTYS 50 mg significantly reduced absolute OFF-time vs placebo: LS mean change -1.98 vs -1.07 hours; placebo-subtracted difference -0.91 hours (95% CI -1.523, -0.287); p=0.008.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥4% and > placebo) were dyskinesia (20% vs 6% placebo), constipation (6% vs 2%), blood creatine kinase increased (5% vs 2%), hypotension/syncope (5% vs 1%), and weight decreased (4% vs 0%). A total of 8% of ONGENTYS 50 mg-treated patients discontinued due to adverse events (vs 6% placebo), most commonly for dyskinesia (3% vs 0.4%).
target_moa: Opicapone is a peripheral catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) inhibitor that blocks peripheral catabolism of levodopa, increasing its bioavailability and availability to the nervous system, thereby reducing OFF-time.
modality: Small molecule (new molecular entity; nitrocatechol COMT inhibitor).

rems.type: No REMS or additional risk management strategies required beyond the recommended labeling.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee input was sought; the application was not referred because this drug is not the first in its class and the safety profile is similar to other approved drugs for this indication.

basis.text: The application received Standard (not Priority) review.

summary.text: Opicapone (Ongentys), a new molecular entity peripheral COMT inhibitor, was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA received April 26, 2019, and reviewed under standard review. Approval was based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials (Studies 301/302) demonstrating substantial evidence of effectiveness; it was approved on the standard pathway with no accelerated approval, no advisory committee, and no REMS.

citations.quote: Opicapone is a new molecular entity and has had marketing authorization for this same indication in the EU since June 2016.
